title: Lee likely to meet Samsung chief for possible discussion on chip projects: sources
summary: President Lee Jae Myung is likely to meet with Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong this week to possibly discuss the country's three mega projects centered on semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI), sources said Monday. The meeting came days after President Lee met with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won. Lee is also likely to have a meeting with Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung this week, the sources said. The talks came amid speculation the United States is demanding South Korean investment in its semiconductor industry as part of Seoul's investment commitment to the country, although Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said earlier that no related talks had been held with Washington.

title: Court grants bail for power broker in 'free opinion poll' case
summary: An appellate court on Monday granted bail for a jailed self-proclaimed power broker convicted for providing free opinion polls to former President Yoon Suk Yeol between 2021 and 2022, legal sources said. The Seoul High Court accepted Myung Tae-kyun's request for bail, about a month after a lower court sentenced him to an 18-month prison term on charges of violating the Political Funds Act. The lower court found Myung guilty of making illegal political contributions by offering the opinion polls for free to Yoon and his wife between June 2021 and March 2022. The district court sentenced Yoon to a two-year prison term in the case. With the Seoul High Court's decision to grant bail, Myung will stand his trial at the appellate court without physical detention.

summary: The government and ruling party are drawing speculation that they are sidelining Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon in their push to expand housing supply. title: Korea opens faster access to NATO standards for defense exporters
summary: Korea’s arms procurement agency has established its first formal procedure for domestic defense companies to obtain NATO standards, a move aimed at helping them compete for contracts and joint development projects in NATO markets. summary: The United States cancelled a joint amphibious landing drill scheduled for next month with South Korea, Seoul's Marine Corps said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on the availability of U.S. forces due to the war in Iran. title: Illegal imports of obesity drugs surge 3.5-fold in Korea
summary: The number of illegally imported obesity treatment drugs detected surged in the first half of this year, driven largely by drugs ordered from foreign websites and shipped through international mail. According to the Korea Customs Service (KCS) Monday, authorities detected 4,155 instances of illegal imports of Mounjaro, Wegovy and other obesity drugs between January and June, nearly 3.5 times the 1,189 cases for all of last year. title: Foreign students in Korea call for support after graduation
summary: With more than 320,000 foreign nationals now studying in Korea, international students say the hardest part may begin when university support ends: finding jobs, changing visas and securing housing on their own. title: Appeals court upholds 18-month prison term for ex-presidential aide over martial law document
summary: An appellate court on Monday upheld an 18-month prison term for a former presidential secretary for drafting a false document linked to former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid. summary: Korea added 292,000 wage jobs in the first quarter of 2026, driven by gains in the health and social welfare, accommodation, and food service sectors, while manufacturing and construction lost ground, official data showed Monday. The number of salaried jobs stood at 20.82 million as of February, up 292,000 from a year earlier, the Ministry of Data and Statistics said. title: DPK leader orders launch of task force to promote political unity
summary: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) leader Kim Min-seok ordered the launch of a task force Monday aimed at achieving broader political unity and expanding cooperation with other parties. "We will build an unbreakable bridge of dialogue with the main opposition People Power Party, and a bridge of political solidarity for the future with progressive and liberal parties," he said. summary: Twelve people have been referred to the prosecution and five others have been red-noticed globally on suspicion of operating an illegal online gambling site, handling over 60 billion won ($43.36 million) in stakes, police said Monday. title: Seoul opens 2nd World Cup Park golf course for outdoor recreation
summary: A new park golf course at World Cup Park will open next week, adding 18 holes to one of Seoul’s largest outdoor recreational facilities and giving residents more room to play amid the city’s green spaces. The Seoul Metropolitan Government will open the second course at Noeul Park on Sept. 1, with reservations beginning Tuesday at 5 p.m. through the Seoul Public Service Reservation System. The 22,000-square-meter course has 18 holes, divided into an A course of nine holes and 535 meters and a B course of nine holes and 575 meters, for a total of 1,110 meters and 66 par. title: Lee's approval rating sinks to new low: poll
summary: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating has slipped to a new low of 40.2 percent, also marking the sixth consecutive week of decline, a poll showed Monday. In the poll conducted on 2,026 voters from Tuesday to Friday by Realmeter and commissioned by the EKN newspaper, Lee's approval rating fell 2.8 percentage points from the previous week. Of the respondents, 56.9 percent gave a negative assessment of Lee's job performance, up 2.8 percentage points from the previous week. title: Is Korea really unsuitable for winemaking? This winemaker in Geochang says no
summary: In the quiet mountain village of Ungyang-myeon, Geochang County, South Gyeongsang Province, sits a modest country home. Beside it are a small winery and a vineyard spanning about 18,000 square meters. Compared with the vast vineyards of Europe’s famous wine regions, the place feels more like a humble Korean grape farm than a grand vineyard. Yet the organically grown grapes harvested here are transformed into Jeong Ssang-eun Wine, a natural wine that has wine lovers across Korea lining up to get their hands on. The winery, run by first-generation grape farmers Jeong Ssang-eun and Lim Hye-sook and their son, second-generation winemaker Jeong Gyu-song, produces only about 9,000 bottles a year due to its small scale.
